notes: Rideshare driver markets. US: Lyft driver regions (lyft.com/driver/cities) plus Uber-only regions; pickupStates are the states a driver registered in that market can accept pickups in, per official sources; where a neighbor state is not confirmed it is excluded (no false events). Baltimore uses the owner-confirmed DMV rule. Outside the US: major cities per app from official city/country lists; unverifiedPlatforms were confirmed only at country level. radiusMi is an app heuristic (50 mi large metro / 35 mi smaller; 50 km / 35 km abroad), not an Uber or Lyft figure. See docs/RIDESHARE_MARKETS.md.

markets.name: Washington DC
markets.fullName: Washington DC / Maryland suburbs / Northern Virginia (DMV)
markets.crossStatePickup: Uber: "Drivers in the DMV area are able to pick up riders in all three states once they meet the requirements for each state." "If you only meet the requirements for one of the states (e.g., only Maryland), you will only be able to accept trip requests within the boundaries of that state." Uber: DC proper pickups need a MD, DC or VA driver's license. Lyft: "Once you're approved, you'll also be able to drive anywhere in Virginia, Maryland,* or Washington, DC." "Drivers without a Washington DC, Maryland, or Virginia driver's license will not be dispatched for pickups in DC proper." Lyft's driver city index lists Alexandria, Arlington, Bethesda-Silver Spring, College Park and Tysons Corner under this region, and its DC page says Lyft is available at DCA and IAD (both in VA).
